neighbours.label: an unidiomatic, superfluous ' the' (or the noun right after it) of the kind non-native writers add before a generic or first-mentioned noun ('due to the factors like …', 'utilizes the radioisotopes for …', 'provide the easy way'); quiet on idiomatic 'the' for something already known. The − pole fires on the matching misused ' a'
fire: Many peoples are facing the problems like the unemployment and the poverty in our country.
This branch of science uses the lasers for the treatment of the various eye disorders.
Our company provides the best and cheap services to the customers who need the help in the shifting.
Nowadays the internet marketing is becoming the popular way to promote the business.
Due to the reasons like the heavy traffic and the smoke, the people are getting the diseases.
The yoga gives the relief from the stress and makes the body flexible.
You should always consult the doctor who will suggest the proper medicines for the treatment.
Solar panels contain the cells which are converting the sunlight into the electricity.
quiet: Many people in our country are facing problems like unemployment and poverty.
This branch of science uses lasers to treat various eye disorders.
Our company offers good, cheap removal services to customers who need help.
Nowadays internet marketing is becoming a popular way to promote a business.
Because of heavy traffic and smoke, people are getting ill more often.
Yoga relieves stress and makes your body more flexible.
I rang the doctor, and the doctor told me to finish the tablets.
She locked the door, put the keys in her bag and walked to the station.

notes: Card: ' the' x21 of the top 32, nearly all in learner-English web text where the article is unneeded or introduces something not yet identified; the − pole's top examples are ' a' in 'identify a cause', 'come to a right place'. Probes: 'due to the factors like' 0.37, 'provide the easy and cheap way' 0.31, 'uses the radio waves for finding' 0.18; idiomatic 'the kettle … the kettle', 'closed the door' 0.01-0.02, the corrected radio-waves sentence 0.00, 'choose the most suitable topic' 0.00 (so a superlative 'the' is not enough). Near misses are the same kind of sentence in idiomatic English, with ordinary 'the'.
